دُعْبُوبٌ , (K, TA,) applied to a man, (TA,) Brisk, lively, or sprightly. (K.) ―
-b2- Stupid, or foolish; as also ↓ أَدْعَبُ , (K, TA,) and ↓ دُعْبُبٌ : (TA:) and stupid, or foolish, and jesting, or joking. (TA.) ―
-b3- Weak, (S, K,) and an object of ridicule. (K.) ―
-b4- Short and ugly and contemptible. (K, * TA.) ―
-b5- I. q. مُخَنَّثٌ, (CK, and so in my MS. copy of the K,) or مُخَنِّثٌ, of the form of the act. part. n., (TA,) [Effeminate, &c.] ―
-b6- Applied to a horse, Tall, or long-bodied; syn. طَوِيلٌ. (K.) ＝
-A2- A road beaten, or trodden, (S, K,) travelled, (TA,) and plain, or conspicuous. (K, TA.) ＝
-A3- A dark night. (K.) ＝
-A4- Black ants; as also ↓ دُعَابَةٌ . (K.) ―
-b2- A certain black esculent grain: or the stem, or root, (أَصْل,) of a certain herb, or leguminous plant, (بَقْلَة,) which is peeled and eaten. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
